questions.title: Likely questions
questions.text:
## Attorney / Trustee
- **How much is it worth?** It depends on the volume and type of records. The buyer makes an offer after reviewing a sample, and any sale can go to the court for approval.
- **What about privacy / PII / HIPAA?** Personal information is removed or de-identified before anything is transferred, so the estate isn't exposed.
- **Does this need court approval?** It can be structured as a sale subject to court approval, like any other estate asset.
- **Who's the buyer?** Established AI training-data companies. I'll share details once we confirm the records fit.
- **Is this legit / who are they?** Established AI training-data companies; I'll share details once we confirm fit. Nothing moves without the estate's sign-off.
- **What formats do they take?** Digital images, video, audio, 3D and CAD files may all be considered. No strict minimum size; the buyer evaluates each case.
- **What do you need from me?** Just a short description of what records the estate has. I handle the rest, so there's minimal administrative burden.
- **How do you get paid?** A finder's fee from the buyer side. There's no cost to the estate.

## Owner
- **How much is it worth?** It depends on how much you have and what kind. The buyer makes an offer after looking at a sample.
- **What about privacy / PII / HIPAA?** Personal and sensitive information is stripped out before anything leaves your hands.
- **Does this need court approval?** No court involved. It's a simple agreement between your company and the buyer.
- **Who's the buyer?** Established AI companies that buy training data. I'll share details once we know your records fit.
- **Is this legit / who are they?** The link is the company's own application page. You apply directly with them, and nothing is shared until they review it.
- **What formats do they take?** Images, video, audio, 3D and CAD files can all count. No strict minimum; they look at each case.
- **What do you need from me?** Just a quick description of what records you have (or apply through the link). I handle the rest.
- **How do you get paid?** A finder's fee from the buyer. It costs you nothing.

gatekeeper.title: Gatekeeper tips
gatekeeper.text:
- Ask for them by first name, confidently: "Hi, is Mark in? It's Amy Sullivan."
- If blocked: "I'm following up on an email I sent [Name] about recovering additional value for [the estate's creditors / the company] from its old records. Could you put me through, or let me know the best way to reach them?"
- Or ask: "Who handles the asset side of the [Company] case?" and get their direct line.
- Never name buyers or quote dollar amounts.

bankruptcy.title: Bankruptcy cheat sheet (general background, not legal advice)
bankruptcy.text:
**Chapter 7 – liquidation.** Business shuts down. Court-appointed TRUSTEE sells assets, pays creditors. Talk to the trustee. Say: "This could add value to the estate for creditors."
**Chapter 11 – reorganization.** Company usually keeps operating and restructures debts under a court-approved PLAN; some are "liquidating 11s" that sell everything. Debts are renegotiated, not erased. Talk to DEBTOR'S COUNSEL. Say: "This could bring extra value into the plan, through a 363 sale with court approval."
**Subchapter V.** Faster, cheaper small-business Chapter 11. Sub V trustee oversees; go through debtor's counsel.
**Chapter 13.** Individuals with wages, not companies. Skip.
## Words
- Estate: everything the debtor owns once in bankruptcy.
- Schedules: debtor's filed asset list; records usually aren't on it ("unscheduled asset").
- 363 sale: court-approved sale of estate assets (a data sale would be one).
- 341 meeting: early creditors' meeting in every case.
- Plan: the Chapter 11 payout plan.
- Creditors / recovery: who gets paid / how much they get back.
